project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer: Develop and test artificial intelligence tools that improve access to climate information or make a sector more resilient to climate hazards.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer: Choose either improved access to climate information or artificial intelligence for a specific sector’s adaptation. Demonstrate a tangible improvement where regional or local authorities will use it.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer: Authorities need climate information they can act on. The sector route also addresses specific operational problems where climate impacts are changing, including in energy.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer: Deliver a tested tool for the selected adaptation need and materials that help authorities and other target users use its outputs.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer: The first route should make climate knowledge more actionable. The second should improve the capacity of selected sectors to respond to climate impacts.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer: Prepare material that helps local or regional authorities use the tools beyond the tests. Reserve resources to cooperate with the European adaptation support platform and practitioner community.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer: The proposal needs at least three independent funded partners in three different eligible countries. At least one must be established in a European Union Member State. The other two must be established in different Member States or countries associated with Horizon Europe (countries formally participating in the European research programme).
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer: Involve regional or local authorities that can test the selected objective. The sector route should include private-sector actors with relevant expertise.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer: Include resources and a mechanism to work with the European adaptation mission implementation platform. Design and test the tools with the authority or sector partners relevant to the chosen objective.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Scope

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer: The group appoints a funded partner to lead the work on regional climate adaptation tools and represent it to the funder.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer: TenneT could coordinate the project if it can contribute sector expertise to the route that applies artificial intelligence to energy-system adaptation. The applicants choose their coordinator (the funded partner that represents the group to the funder).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 5, 11–13 · B — Eligibility
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Scope

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer: TenneT could take part in regional climate adaptation tools without receiving a grant. As an associated partner (an organisation that works without a grant), it could contribute sector expertise to the route that applies artificial intelligence to energy-system adaptation. It would cover its own costs and would not count towards the minimum number of funded partners.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 5, 11–13 · B — Eligibility
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Scope

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer: TenneT can receive up to 100% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow) for qualifying work. The Dutch entity could contribute sector expertise to the route that applies artificial intelligence to energy-system adaptation. The rate helps set a lump sum (a fixed grant paid for accepted work rather than reimbursing actual spending).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Scope

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer: TenneT could use data and virtual asset models to validate an electricity infrastructure adaptation tool in several authorities’ territories.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Scope

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer: Improve an existing tool where it can meet the need, or justify developing a new tool. Show the concrete benefit to the authorities or sector users.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Scope

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer: Innovate in how authorities access and interpret climate data, or in an application that changes how an exposed sector adapts.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Scope

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer: Identify a tool or gap, develop or adapt the application, and test it with the authorities or within the required territories.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer: Test the climate-information route with at least three regional or local authorities. Test the sector route across at least five regional or local authority territories.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer: Build on relevant European climate data, existing tools and the Mission platform (the support network for regional adaptation). For the sector route, fit the tool to users’ actual decisions.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Scope

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer: Show concrete added value for participating authorities or demonstrate a sectoral adaptation benefit in the required territories. Consider bias and limitations in the data and models.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?
cards.answer: Test the data-access route with at least three regional or local authorities. Test the sector route in at least five such territories and involve businesses with relevant sector expertise.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Scope

cards.title: Safety and cybersecurity
cards.question: Which safety, cybersecurity or data requirements must the project meet?
cards.answer: Consider representativeness and potential biases in data and results. Address the limitations and risk of misinformation if the tool uses generative artificial intelligence (models that can produce new content).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Specific conditions

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
The Commission indicates EUR 12 million for regional climate adaptation tools. It expects 4 awards.
- Grant request: around EUR 3 million per project. Different requests remain eligible.
- Funding form: Lump sum (a fixed grant paid for accepted work rather than reimbursing actual spending).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · p. 22 · Overview of this call
Researching and applying the potential of Artificial Intelligence to foster climate resilience at the regional and local levels · Budget overview

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer: The grant can cover up to 100% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow) for regional climate adaptation tools. This is a research and innovation action (a grant for research and early development). The rate is used to calculate the lump sum (a fixed grant paid for accepted work rather than reimbursing actual spending).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
Plan the budget for regional climate adaptation tools using the cost categories allowed by the grant. Use estimates to set the fixed grant.
- Budget detail: Set out the main cost categories by beneficiary (organisations formally responsible for funded work) and work package (separately planned blocks of project work).
- Purchases and subcontracting: Apply best-value and conflict-of-interest rules.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents
Lump Sum Funding in Horizon Europe: What do I need to know? · pp. 6–7, 26–27 · Detailed budget table

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
Plan cash flow for regional climate adaptation tools around acceptance of completed blocks of work.
- Payment model: Pre-financing (an advance at the start of the grant), then periodic payments for accepted work packages (separately planned blocks of project work) and a final balance.
- Retention or guarantee: 5–8% of the maximum grant is deducted from pre-financing for mutual insurance.
- Financial reporting or audit: Keep evidence of implementation and completion.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 33 · Reporting & payment arrangements
Lump Sum Funding in Horizon Europe: What do I need to know? · pp. 17–23 · Payment schedule, Reporting and payment, Keeping records

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
Apply for regional climate adaptation tools through the European Funding & Tenders Portal in one stage.
- Full proposal: 21 September 2027 at 17:00 Brussels time. The technical proposal (Part B) is limited to 45 pages.
- Opening: 9 February 2027.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · p. 22 · Overview of this call
Researching and applying the potential of Artificial Intelligence to foster climate resilience at the regional and local levels · General information
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 3–4 · A — Admissibility
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules) sets the start date and duration for regional climate adaptation tools.
- Required start: Work normally starts after the grant agreement is signed. A reasoned exception needs approval.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 30–31 · Starting date & project duration

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
The Commission’s timetable for assessing and contracting regional climate adaptation tools is indicative.
- Expected invitation or assessment result: Around 5 months from the full-proposal deadline.
- Grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules): Around 8 months from the full-proposal deadline.
- Conditions before starting: Beneficiaries (organisations formally responsible for funded work) must conclude a written consortium agreement (the partners’ written agreement on how the project will run).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 30 · Indicative timetable for evaluation and for signature of the grant agreement
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium agreement

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
Use the portal’s forms to submit the proposal and supporting documents for regional climate adaptation tools.
- Application form: Complete Part A in the Portal and attach Part B and mandatory annexes.
- Registration: Beneficiaries (organisations formally responsible for funded work) and affiliated entities (organisations legally linked to funded partners) need participant identification codes (organisation registration numbers).
- Partner documents: The coordinator confirms its authority to act for the applicant group.
- Budget: Provide the detailed lump-sum (a fixed grant paid for accepted work rather than reimbursing actual spending) budget table with the full proposal.
- Mandatory application input: Identify Objective 1 or 2 in the proposal's free keywords.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 4–5, 11–13 · B — Eligibility
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Scope

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Regional climate adaptation tools proposals compete on research quality, impact and the quality of the delivery plan.
- Full proposal: Excellence, impact and implementation are scored. Each criterion needs 3/5 and the total needs 10/15.
- If thresholds are met, the portfolio should include the highest-ranked proposal for each of the two objectives.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 23–26 · D — Award criteria
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
Name the selected climate-adaptation objective in the proposal so it can be ranked in the right group.
- Conditional requirement: Choose a single objective. Show how the proposed artificial intelligence approach improves on existing options or substantiate the need for a new solution.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 61–63 · Specific conditions
